author: agent:claude-code
message: Turn off Tailscale SSH on vgsquid-jade (node sharing for colleagues) and make the tailscale module's ssh switch declarative both ways. (proposal 01a15dbc-8318-76b9-ad69-a2a6e3a584bc, proposed by agent:claude-code, accepted by user)

text: No Tailscale SSH on vgsquid-jade: colleagues come in by node share, so login is OpenSSH
why: The user chose node sharing for colleagues (only vgsquid-jade is shared, from the admin console; they accept it with their own Tailscale accounts, see nothing else of the tailnet and take no seats) over inviting them into the tailnet (they'd reach every other device unless ACLs restrict them, and count as users on the plan). With Tailscale SSH on, tailscaled answers port 22 on the tailnet address and judges each connection by the tailnet's SSH policy, which can never match a shared-in user, so they would be refused before reaching OpenSSH. jade sets modules.tailscale.ssh = false; everyone, the owner included, logs in through OpenSSH with a key (core.headless.guests, core.headless.sshd.authorizedKeys). To verify with the first colleague.

text: The ssh switch sets Tailscale SSH both ways (--ssh=true|false)
why: extraSetFlags was `--ssh` only when on, so turning the option off left a host that had once run `tailscale up --ssh` (or `tailscale set --ssh`) still advertising it. tailscaled-set now runs `tailscale set --ssh=<bool>` at every boot, so the option is the state either way. Checked: jade evaluates to --ssh=false, and with the switch forced on to --ssh=true; `tailscale set --help` lists --ssh=false.
